messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
Mostly, I want working coffee again without this turning into a fight. I’m not sure whether A and B are okay with you contacting them directly; you’d need to check with them.

I know the machine means a lot to B, but the leak does worry me, and I’d prefer something simpler that needs little upkeep. I’m pretty worn out after work, so I couldn’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I’m fine with you sharing that.

I want it repaired and kept, but the constant breakages are wearing me down, and I’ve got little time—any repair or discussion needs to fit into short slots. It was Dad’s, so replacing it isn’t just a practical choice for me. You can relay that to A and C.
Yes, that’s about right. I’d put it as wanting a reliable, low-maintenance setup. I don’t think I have anything else to add just now.
Yes, that’s it. I want to keep it, but I need it to work without constantly eating up my time. Nothing else to add.
Mostly. I want working coffee without a fight, but I wouldn’t put it as needing to keep their relationship warm—that’s for them to work out. I’m glad you can contact them directly.
Yes, that fits. I can weigh in on options, but I don’t have the bandwidth to coordinate or handle repairs.
Thanks, that sounds thoughtful. I appreciate not rushing anyone, and nothing feels off to me at the moment.
That’s fine. Just keep discussions to short slots; I don’t have much spare time.
Yes, that fits. I can weigh in, but I can’t take on coordinating or repairs.

Option 3 sounds best to me: a simpler machine with less upkeep. I’d be a little uneasy about options 1 and 2 leaving us relying on the old machine, even with a repair. I know it’s important to B, though.

Option 2 is the only one I’d support. A professional repair, with a clear agreed period and a simple replacement trigger, gives it a fair chance without leaving me managing every breakdown. Option 1 leaves too much uncertainty; option 3 takes it out of the office before trying to keep it going. I’m not comfortable calling option 2 settled until the period and trigger are agreed.
Option 2 seems reassuring, though the fallback terms still need agreement. My main discomfort is that option 1 relies on the old machine staying reliable. I don’t want to choose for A or B.
